exposure: Patient positioning during spinal anesthesia induction (lateral position)
Patient positioning during spinal anesthesia induction (sitting position)
cohort: The study included 100 parturients undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia, split into two groups based on positioning during anesthesia induction.
finding: The lateral position for spinal anesthesia in cesarean sections resulted in faster sensory block onset, longer motor block duration, and reduced maternal hypotension compared to the sitting position, with comparable neonatal Apgar scores.
